data.long_meaning: In the Bible, the name Moises (Moses) is derived from the Hebrew word mosheh, which means ‘drawn out’. God appeared to Moses in a burning bush and commanded him to lead the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt. This name is a reminder of God’s deliverance of His people and the courage and faith of Moses in following God’s call.
data.etymology: Moises belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Drawn out of the water.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Moises total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

data.cultural_impact: The name Moises or Moses holds immense cultural significance in Judaism, Christianity, and even Islam. In Christianity, Moises is revered as a prophet and appears in the Old Testament. He is depicted as a leader, shepherd, and prophet who led the Israelites out of slavery in Egypt with God’s help. Moises is also significant as a symbol of liberation and a shining example of faith and courage.
data.spiritual_significance: The name Moises or Moses has deep spiritual significance, representing deliverance, faith, and obedience to God. It is a reminder of God’s power to save and free His people, even in the most difficult circumstances. Moises’s story inspires us to follow God’s call, have faith in His plan, and trust in His power to bring us through our challenges. This name is a powerful reminder of God’s love, faithfulness, and providence.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Moises, meaning "drawn out of the water" in Hebrew, symbolizes God's intervention in saving the infant Moses from the Nile river, setting him on a path to lead the Israelites out of Egyptian slavery. Spiritually, it is a reminder of God's salvation and guidance in challenging circumstances.

biblical_reference.note: The name Moses is mentioned throughout the Bible as a central figure in the Israelites' deliverance from Egypt.

historical_references.reference: Historical records show that Moses led the Israelites out of Egypt and received the Ten Commandments on Mount Sinai. The name Moises carried significant spiritual weight in that era.
historical_references.context: Old Testament of the Bible, Book of Exodus
